questions.prompt: An AI gives you a quotation and says it came from an official safety manual. You cannot find the quotation in the manual. What should you do?
choices: Use it because the AI sounded certain.
Treat it as unverified and do not quote it until you find the original source.
Ask the AI to invent a page number.
Put quotation marks around it anyway.
questions.explanation: A quotation needs a real, traceable source. AI can fabricate quotations and citations.

questions.prompt: An AI answer about an FRC rule is based on a 2025 manual, but your team is preparing for the 2027 season. What is the best response?
choices: Use the old rule unless someone complains.
Verify the current-season manual and updates before acting.
Average the two seasons together.
Assume rules never change.
questions.explanation: Robotics rules, software, and safety requirements can change. Currency is part of verification.

questions.prompt: Which actions strengthen verification of an important AI-generated claim? Select all that apply.
choices: Check an authoritative primary source.
Compare with an independent reliable source.
Ask the same model repeatedly until it agrees with itself.
Check the date and context of the source.
questions.explanation: Verification means using evidence outside the model and checking that the evidence is current and relevant.

questions.prompt: Two teachers at the same school have different AI rules for assignments. Which rule should you follow?
choices: Whichever rule allows more AI.
The rule for the specific class and assignment.
Your robotics team's rule instead.
Whatever your friends are doing.
questions.explanation: Permitted assistance can vary by teacher, course, and assignment. The applicable instructions control.

questions.prompt: Your teacher requires disclosure of generative AI use. You used AI to reorganize your outline and suggest counterarguments. What should you do?
choices: Hide it because the final words are yours.
Disclose the assistance in the form the teacher requires.
Claim another student helped instead.
Delete the assignment.
questions.explanation: When disclosure is required, accurately describe meaningful AI assistance.

questions.prompt: Which use is most likely to support learning rather than replace it?
choices: Submitting an AI-written lab conclusion without reading it.
Asking AI to quiz you, then checking missed concepts against class materials.
Having AI take an online test for you.
Using AI to fabricate a source list.
questions.explanation: AI can be useful as a tutor or practice partner when the student remains engaged in the learning.

questions.prompt: AI proposes a new autonomous routine that could drive the robot close to people during testing. What should happen before a full-speed run?
choices: Run it immediately to save time.
Use controlled testing, safety procedures, review, and appropriate supervision.
Trust the simulator completely.
Ask AI whether anyone will get hurt.
questions.explanation: Physical systems require staged testing and human safety controls. AI confidence is not a safety validation.

questions.prompt: An AI recommends wiring a sensor at 12 V, but the manufacturer's datasheet says its input is 5 V maximum. Which source controls?
choices: The AI because it explained the answer better.
The manufacturer's current datasheet.
Whichever value is higher.
A random forum comment.
questions.explanation: For component limits, current authoritative technical documentation is the source to follow.

questions.prompt: An AI scouting model ranks a team very low, but several match records are missing. What is the responsible interpretation?
choices: Treat the rank as precise.
Recognize the uncertainty, investigate missing data, and avoid overclaiming confidence.
Delete the team's good matches.
Assume missing data means zero performance.
questions.explanation: Data quality affects model output. Missing or biased data should reduce confidence in a ranking.

questions.prompt: A teammate creates the original CAD concept and you use AI to improve documentation for it. How should the work be represented?
choices: Claim you designed the concept because you wrote the documentation.
Credit the teammate's design work and accurately describe your own contribution.
Credit only the AI.
Remove all names.
questions.explanation: AI assistance does not erase human contributions. Credit should reflect who actually did what.

questions.prompt: AI adds a claim that Team 1555 mentored 300 students, but the team has no evidence that happened. What should you do?
choices: Keep it because it sounds impressive.
Remove or correct the claim and use only supportable facts.
Change 300 to 299.
Ask the AI to make the story more convincing.
questions.explanation: AI-generated fabrication is still fabrication. Team claims should be truthful and supportable.

questions.prompt: A mentor shares a confidential draft recommendation letter and asks for feedback. Is it appropriate to paste the entire letter into a public AI service without permission?
choices: Yes, because AI is not a person.
No; confidential material should not be uploaded to an external service without permission and an approved data-handling basis.
Yes, if you delete it afterward.
Only if the letter is long.
questions.explanation: Confidentiality and consent still matter when using AI services.

questions.prompt: An AI ranking system does not use race or income directly, but heavily weights ZIP code. Why could that still create fairness concerns?
choices: ZIP codes are always random.
A seemingly neutral feature can act as a proxy for protected or socioeconomic characteristics.
Computers cannot be biased.
Fairness only matters if the code contains an insult.
questions.explanation: Proxy variables can reproduce disparities even when sensitive attributes are not directly included.

questions.prompt: Which practices support more inclusive AI use? Select all that apply.
choices: Test outputs with diverse examples.
Provide a way for people to question or appeal important automated decisions.
Assume one language or communication style represents everyone.
Consider accessibility for users with disabilities.
questions.explanation: Inclusive design tests across different users and preserves human review, accessibility, and recourse.

questions.prompt: Why is human review especially important when AI affects scholarships, discipline, hiring, or other high-impact decisions?
choices: Humans are never biased.
AI can make errors or reproduce unfair patterns, and accountable people must be able to review context and correct outcomes.
It makes the computer faster.
It guarantees everyone gets the same result.
questions.explanation: High-impact decisions need accountable review, context, and a path to correct mistakes.

questions.prompt: You accidentally paste an API token into an AI chat. What is the safest next action?
choices: Ignore it if nobody replies.
Revoke or rotate the token promptly and follow team security procedures.
Post the token in Slack so everyone knows.
Rename the token.
questions.explanation: A disclosed credential should be treated as potentially compromised and rotated or revoked.

questions.prompt: You want AI help summarizing student feedback. Which approach best follows data minimization?
choices: Upload names, phone numbers, addresses, and feedback even if only the comments are needed.
Remove unnecessary identifying information and share only what the task requires.
Add more personal data to improve context.
Publish the raw file first.
questions.explanation: Data minimization means using only the information actually needed for the task.

questions.prompt: Which actions align with strong account security? Select all that apply.
choices: Use unique passwords.
Enable multifactor authentication where available.
Keep systems and software updated.
Reuse one easy password everywhere.
questions.explanation: Unique passwords, MFA, and updates are core protections for school and team accounts.

questions.prompt: You can make a convincing AI voice clone of a teammate for a joke. What should you consider first?
choices: Whether the clone is funny enough.
Consent, potential harm, deception, and how the recording could spread beyond the joke.
Whether the teammate owns a phone.
Whether the model is free.
questions.explanation: Technical ability does not equal permission. Consent and foreseeable harm matter.

questions.prompt: You receive a panicked call that sounds like a family member asking for money immediately. What is a strong verification step?
choices: Send money before the caller hangs up.
Contact the family member through a known number or another trusted channel before acting.
Trust the voice because it sounds exact.
Give the caller account passwords.
questions.explanation: Voice cloning can make emergency scams sound authentic. Verify through an independent known channel.

questions.prompt: A dramatic AI-generated image is clearly labeled as fictional by its creator, but someone reposts it without the label as real news. What changed?
choices: Nothing; context never matters.
Removing provenance and context can turn creative content into misinformation.
The image becomes copyrighted automatically.
The pixels change.
questions.explanation: Context and provenance affect how media is interpreted. Stripping labels can make synthetic media deceptive.

questions.prompt: Another team asks for help with a programming issue you solved using AI. What is the best way to help?
choices: Share an untested answer as guaranteed correct.
Share what worked, explain any uncertainty, and help them verify and understand it.
Refuse because helping competitors is always wrong.
Hide a dangerous bug in the code.
questions.explanation: Responsible Coopertition combines helpfulness with honesty, quality, and safety.

questions.prompt: Helping another team does not mean you should share which of the following?
choices: A public link to official documentation.
A general explanation of a programming concept.
Private credentials, personal student data, or information you are not authorized to disclose.
A verified safety reminder.
questions.explanation: Coopertition does not override privacy, security, or authorization boundaries.

questions.prompt: After giving another team AI-assisted advice, you discover the advice was wrong. What best reflects Gracious Professionalism?
choices: Say nothing so you do not look bad.
Correct the information promptly and explain what changed.
Blame the other team.
Delete your messages and deny helping.
questions.explanation: Owning and correcting mistakes protects others and models professional integrity.
